body.estimand_functional: Unconditionally, \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\gtrsim R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal M_H\), and \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}\gtrsim [n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}]\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal P_K\). The matching relation \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal M_H\) is conditional on an affirmative full-fiber occupancy lift.

sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed target-fiber mechanism profiles over the full propensity and control-regression Hölder classes; no named nuisance estimator and no fixed finite nuisance sieve is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate on a bounded-design-density class, with the upper construction in Section 5.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The bounded-density superclass lower-frontier theorem, for the converse direction only

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section 4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems 1 and 3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Theorems 1--2 and the adaptive lower bound characterize extra logarithmic costs for pointwise federated-private density adaptation.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition 2 and Section 4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

body.tldr: The unconditional results are the exact occupancy-amplification identity and the sparse- and dense-cell pure-private lower branches on the exact-uniform Hölder class \(\mathcal M_H\). Since \(\mathcal M_H\) is a strict subclass of Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-design-density class \(\mathcal P_K\), minimax monotonicity transfers the full converse, including the published nonprivate floor, to \(\mathcal P_K\). A matching upper bound on \(\mathcal M_H\) remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift; no upper bound is transferred to \(\mathcal P_K\), and smoothness adaptation remains open with no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty claimed.

project_justification.gap: No located result gives a pure-central-DP minimax frontier for pointwise CATE with unknown smooth propensity and outcome regression. The closest banked construction uses only exactly-two-record cells and therefore loses all signal when cell occupancy diverges.
project_justification.niche: Realized cell occupancy can amplify a degenerate nuisance-product signal while preserving constant record influence, potentially joining the sparse \(n^2\epsilon\) branch to the dense \(n\epsilon\) branch with no third radius.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact occupancy identity and the sparse and dense pure-private lower branches on the exact-uniform class, then transfers the complete converse upward to Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-density class by subclass monotonicity. Matching attainment on the exact-uniform class still requires the unresolved nuisance-independent full-fiber score, and adaptation remains a separate open problem with no asserted penalty.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman establish the nonprivate pointwise-CATE frontier on a larger bounded-design-density Hölder class. This work proves the occupancy identity and both pure-private lower branches on the strict exact-uniform subclass \(\mathcal M_H\); because every exact-uniform law is in Kennedy et al.'s class \(\mathcal P_K\), the nonprivate floor and both privacy converse branches transfer upward, but no upper bound does. Zeng et al. motivate conditioning on occupancy, Chaudhuri et al. motivate stable private projection statistics, and Acharya et al. supply the Hamming-coupling inequality used in the converse; none supplies the unresolved full-class CATE score. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound templates only for a separate open adaptation question, so no CATE adaptation rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed here. The remaining cited work concerns testing, approximate-private CATE release, sparse-versus-dense representations, and nonprivate random-design geometry rather than a matching pure-private upper frontier for this model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The identity in Lemma 2 does not itself solve the full-fiber problem. For arbitrary least-favorable priors, the second-order kernel orientation can depend on a growing nuisance profile, and clipping local projections can reintroduce a sieve-size factor. The proposed early kill test is the finite \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\) two-resolution program from the parent archive: impose every replacement-neighbor constraint, increase both occupancy and nuisance-sign dimension, and reject the route if the optimized weighted-shell functional grows with the nuisance dimension after occupancy weighting.
body.honest_scope: The unconditional scope is fixed-smoothness inference under the exact-uniform design: the occupancy-amplification identity and both pure-private lower branches hold on \(\mathcal M_H\). The resulting converse transfers to Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-density class \(\mathcal P_K\) solely by superclass monotonicity. The matching upper bound remains conditional and exact-uniform because the nuisance-independent full-fiber occupancy lift is unresolved; transfer of that upper bound to a bounded-density design is not claimed. Smoothness adaptation is a separate open question, with neither an adaptive rate nor a logarithmic penalty asserted.
